title: Ice Age Spear Points Tell a Fascinating Story of Human Progress - Nautilus
gist: Anthropologists from the University of Mississippi and University of Alabama studied stone spear tips from two hunter-gatherer groups who settled the Tennessee River Valley in different periods, showing that the value placed on tools shifts with circumstances.

insights.claim: The value people place on possessions is contingent on circumstances: stranded in wilderness, a phone becomes useless and cash becomes fire tinder while a sweatpants drawstring becomes a fishing line or snare.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A reminder that asset value is regime-dependent — utility, not price, dominates when infrastructure (power, networks) disappears.
insights.quote: The value we place on things is contingent on our circumstances and subject to change as they do.
insights.locator: Imagine you’re suddenly transported to the wilderness

insights.so_what: Frames technology adoption and discard as circumstance-driven — a long-run analog for how changing environments reprice tools.
